chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): What is the waiting period (iddah) of the Mut'ah woman if the husband from whom she enjoyed dies? He said: Four months and ten days. He then said: O Zurarah, in all marriages, if the husband dies, the waiting period for the woman is four months and ten days, whether she was free or a slave, and regardless of whether the marriage was Mut'ah, permanent marriage (Tazwij), or ownership by right (of a concubine). The waiting period of the divorced woman is three months, and for the slave woman who is divorced, it is half of what is upon the free woman, and likewise for the Mut'ah woman, it is what is upon the slave woman.

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعَةِ: The woman in a temporary marriage (Mut'ah)

ai.seo_question: What is the iddah (waiting period) for a woman in a Mut'ah marriage if her husband dies?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfahani, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that the iddah for a woman in a temporary marriage (Mut'ah) upon her husband's death is four months and ten days, aligning with the general rule for widows. The narration further distinguishes the waiting periods for free versus slave women and those who are divorced, emphasizing the consistency of the four-month-and-ten-day period across different marital statuses when the husband dies. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the equivalence of Mut'ah and permanent marriage in terms of inheritance and waiting periods upon death.
